title: Causal & Reason Words - Explaining Why
description: Learn to explain reasons and causes: parce que (because), car (for), puisque (since), comme (as), grâce à (thanks to), à cause de (because of)
can_do: Explain why things happen (because, since, thanks to)
Give reasons for your actions and decisions
Connect cause and effect in French

vocabulary.note: question word - answer with parce que

concepts.example: {Je mange parce que j'ai faim} (I eat because I'm hungry), {Je ne viens pas parce que je suis malade} (I'm not coming because I'm sick)

concepts.definition: More formal than '{parce que}', CANNOT start a sentence, common in writing
concepts.example: {On étudie le français car c'est beau} (We study French for it's beautiful), {Je prends un café car je suis fatigué} (I'm having a coffee for I'm tired)

concepts.definition: Indicates logical conclusion or something already known, slightly formal
concepts.example: {Puisque tu es là, on commence} (Since you're here, we'll start), {Puisque c'est vrai, je te crois} (Since it's true, I believe you)

concepts.definition: Explains reason, MUST come at beginning of sentence
concepts.example: {Comme il fait beau, on va au parc} (As it's nice, we're going to the park), {Comme je suis fatigué, je vais dormir} (As I'm tired, I'm going to sleep)

concepts.definition: Positive attribution, followed by a noun or pronoun
concepts.example: {Grâce à toi}, {je comprends mieux} (Thanks to you, I understand better), {Grâce au professeur}, {je parle bien} (Thanks to the teacher, I speak well)

concepts.definition: Often negative or neutral, followed by a noun (NOT a clause!)
concepts.example: {À cause de la musique, je ne peux pas travailler} (Because of the music, I can't work), {À cause du bus, je suis en retard} (Because of the bus, I'm late)

items.text: Je ne viens pas ___ je suis malade
items.gloss: I'm not coming because I'm sick

mistakes.feedback: Car works here! But '{parce que}' is more natural in spoken French.
Grâce à is for positive reasons + NOUN: '{grâce à toi}'. Use '{parce que}' + clause here.
À cause de needs a NOUN: '{à cause de la maladie}'. Use '{parce que}' + clause here.

items.text: On étudie le français ___ c'est beau
items.gloss: We study French for it's beautiful

mistakes.feedback: Parce que works! But '{car}' is more elegant in this context.
Comme must come at the START of the sentence: '{Comme c'est utile, on étudie...}'

items.text: ___ il fait beau, on va au parc
items.gloss: As it's nice, we're going to the park

mistakes.feedback: Parce que doesn't typically start sentences. Use '{Comme}' at the beginning!
Car CANNOT start a sentence! Use '{Comme}' at the beginning.
Comme works! But '{puisque}' is perfect for logical conclusions.
Parce que is less natural at the start. Use '{puisque}' for 'since'.

items.gloss: Thanks to you, I understand better

mistakes.feedback: Parce que needs a CLAUSE (subject + verb). Use '{grâce à}' + noun here!
À cause de is for negative/neutral! Use '{grâce à}' for positive thanks.

items.text: ___ la musique, je ne peux pas travailler
items.gloss: Because of the music, I can't work

mistakes.feedback: Parce que needs a CLAUSE: '{parce qu'il pleut}'. Use '{à cause de}' + noun here!
Grâce à is for POSITIVE reasons! Use '{à cause de}' for negative/neutral.

items.text: Pourquoi tu ne viens pas ? - ___ je suis fatigué
items.gloss: Why aren't you coming? - Because I'm tired

mistakes.feedback: Car works but sounds formal. Use '{parce que}' to answer '{pourquoi}'.
Puisque is for known facts, not direct answers to '{pourquoi}'. Use '{parce que}'!

items.gloss: I'm late because of the bus

mistakes.feedback: Parce que needs a CLAUSE: '{parce qu'il y a du traffic}'. Use '{à cause de}' + noun!
Being late isn't positive! Use '{à cause de}' for negative reasons.

items.gloss: I understand thanks to the teacher

mistakes.feedback: Close! But '{grâce à}' + noun is more elegant than 'parce que' + clause here.
Succeeding is positive! Use '{grâce à}' for positive attribution.

items.text: Il ne travaille pas ___ il est riche
items.gloss: He doesn't work because he's rich

mistakes.feedback: Parce que works! But '{car}' sounds more sophisticated here.
Comme must be at the START: '{Comme il est riche, il ne travaille pas}'.

items.text: ___ du travail, je ne peux pas venir
items.gloss: Because of work, I can't come

mistakes.feedback: Bad weather isn't positive! Use '{à cause de}' for negative reasons.
Parce que needs a CLAUSE: '{parce qu'il fait mauvais}'. Use '{à cause de}' + noun!

items.text: On va partir ___ tu es là

mistakes.feedback: Parce que works! But '{puisque}' emphasizes the logical conclusion better.
Car works but '{puisque}' is more natural for 'since'.

items.text: ___ c'est ton anniversaire, on va au restaurant
items.gloss: Since/As it's your birthday, we're going to a restaurant

mistakes.feedback: Parce que rarely starts sentences. Use '{Comme}' at the beginning!
Puisque works! But '{Comme}' is more natural here.

items.gloss: I love you because you're kind

mistakes.feedback: Car works! But '{parce que}' is more natural in speech.
Grâce à needs a NOUN, not a clause. Use '{parce que}' here!

items.text: On parle français ___ on est en France
items.gloss: We speak French since we're in France

mistakes.feedback: Parce que works! Both are correct, but '{car}' is slightly more formal.
Puisque works! All three work here actually.

items.text: ___ mon aide, tu as fini à temps
items.gloss: Thanks to my help, you finished on time

mistakes.feedback: Parce que needs a CLAUSE. Use '{grâce à}' + noun for attribution!
Finishing on time is positive! Use '{grâce à}' for positive reasons.
Close! But '{à cause de}' + noun is more direct than parce que + clause.
Not sleeping well isn't positive! Use '{à cause de}' for problems.

items.text: ___ j'ai le temps, je vais t'aider
items.gloss: Since I have time, I'm going to help you

mistakes.feedback: Parce que rarely starts sentences. '{Comme}' is perfect at the start!
Puisque works! Both comme and puisque work here.
